Face à la recrudescence des tentatives d: Faced with the resurgence of online fraud attempts, notably identity theft and the creation of fake websites, Poste Algérie has announced a series of reinforced measures to protect its customers. These actions are part of a context marked by the increase of cyber threats in Algeria, where telecom operators (Mobilis, Djezzy, Ooredoo) and public institutions are increasingly targeted.
Une réponse structurée aux cybermenaces: A structured response to rising cyber threats
La Société postale algérienne (SPA) a of: The Société postale algérienne (SPA) has formalized the adoption of a multidimensional action plan aimed at securing its customers against online fraud. This system, developed by the Information Systems Security Directorate (DSSI), is structured around four main pillars: technical, legal, informational, and awareness-raising. A comprehensive approach that reflects the evolution of threats in a rapidly changing Algerian digital ecosystem.
Surveillance accrue des faux sites et us: Increased monitoring of fake sites and identity theft
Dans un communiqué rendu public, Poste A: In a public statement, Poste Algérie revealed that its DSSI conducts regular monitoring of fraudulent platforms, notably websites and pages impersonating its identity. This initiative comes at a time when cybercriminals are increasingly targeting public institutions and telecom operators in Algeria. In 2023, cases of identity theft had already been reported, notably via fake sites imitating the interfaces of Mobilis, Djezzy, or Ooredoo, prompting users to disclose their personal or banking data.
La coordination avec les autorités compé: Coordination with competent authorities, including the National Gendarmerie and the Judicial Police, is reinforced to track down these illicit activities. An essential collaboration in a country where the Internet penetration rate exceeds 70%, according to the latest data from ARPT (Post and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority).
Poste Algérie appelle les citoyens victi: Poste Algérie calls on citizens who are victims of or exposed to fraud to act quickly by visiting one of the 1,500 post offices distributed across the territory or by contacting the toll-free number 1530. A measure that adds to the obligation to file a complaint with regional security authorities, a crucial step to enable law enforcement to trace criminal networks.
\"La sensibilisation reste notre meilleu: "Awareness remains our best tool," said an SPA official speaking on condition of anonymity. "We regularly organize prevention campaigns, notably via social networks and local media, to alert our customers to the methods used by fraudsters."
Contexte algérien : un écosystème numéri: Algerian context: a digital ecosystem under pressure
L’Algérie, avec ses 48 millions d’abonné: Algeria, with its 48 million mobile subscribers (including 25 million for Djezzy, 15 million for Ooredoo, and 8 million for Mobilis), is fertile ground for cyber threats. Telecom operators, already on the front line against phishing or smishing attacks, are strengthening their own security systems. In 2022, Ooredoo Algeria, for example, launched a platform dedicated to fraud detection, while Djezzy collaborated with the Bank of Algeria to secure mobile transactions.
La SPA, en tant qu’institution historiqu: SPA, as a historical institution, plays a key role in this dynamic. With over 12 million customer accounts, it must now contend with unprecedented technological and regulatory challenges, particularly following the adoption of Law No. 23-15 on cybersecurity, which stiffens penalties against cybercriminals.
Face à cette situation, Poste Algérie et: Faced with this situation, Poste Algérie and Algerian cybersecurity experts provide several tips for citizens:
Vérifier systématiquement l’URL des site: Systematically check the URL of websites before entering any sensitive data.
Ne jamais communiquer ses identifiants p: Never share your login credentials via email, SMS, or phone call.
Utiliser des mots de passe complexes et: Use complex passwords and enable two-factor authentication whenever possible.
Signaler toute tentative de fraude via l: Report any fraud attempts through official channels (1530 or post offices).
\"La vigilance est de mise, surtout avec: "Vigilance is required, especially with the rise of online services," recalls an Algiers-based cybersecurity expert. "Fraudsters often exploit user vulnerabilities, hence the importance of digital education."
Perspectives : vers une stratégie nation: Outlook: towards a national cybersecurity strategy?
Alors que l’Algérie ambitionne de deveni: As Algeria aims to become a digital hub in Africa, the fight against online fraud is becoming a strategic issue. Discussions are underway to harmonize efforts between telecom operators, banks, and public institutions, similar to the initiatives led in the EU with the GDPR. A coordinated approach that could ultimately position Algeria as a key cybersecurity player in the Mediterranean.
